Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:61: Further, regarding the greatness of one who guards his eyes, the verse in Parashat Kedoshim explains it in saying, "Do not turn to idols..." (Leviticus 19:4), and we have already explained, from Rashbi, that this warning was said regarding a person not looking at women. Behold, its greatness is to cause the Shechinah to rest with him — this is what it says, "I am the Lord your God" — the mention of the Name Elohim indicates this: that "I am your God" resting upon you, if you are careful in this. Further, it is a rebuke to a person to guard his sight, for by blemishing his sight he makes himself an idol, as it is said, "nor make for yourselves molten gods" — precisely as explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and we shall further explain this below, please God; it is far better that a person make himself a vessel in which holiness may rest, and not the reverse, God forbid. It is further possible that these three words, "I am the Lord your God," correspond to the Name Yavak, alluded to in the three colors of the eye, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Tikkunei Zohar 128a), whose wording we quoted at the beginning of the chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:62: Proof for this teaching, that the Shechinah is with whoever guards his sight, was testified to me by a certain Torah scholar, who said he saw, in the kingdom of the Maghreb (Morocco), a certain pious sage who never raises his eyes from the ground, being always humble of eye; and out of the greatness of his piety, whoever provoked him would not complete his year [of life]; and further miraculous events occurred to him, which I shall not elaborate on here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:63: And with this, this chapter is completed:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:1: This chapter will explain the rectification of hearing and smell. Regarding the rectification of hearing, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote, in the Gate of Separation (ch. 5), in these words: and strive further to seal your ear from hearing what you do not need, and separate from excessive talk, falsehood, gossip, and evil speech, and separate from what will bring you to rebel against God and abandon His commandments — such as the various kinds of music, song, laughter, and singing that distract you from the commandments and good deeds; but incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, as it is said, "an ear that hears the reproof of life" (Proverbs 15:31) — so far his words. His words, peace be upon him, are brief and general, and need to be detailed and explained. Likewise one must distance oneself from hearing the voice of a woman singing, for "a woman's voice is nakedness" (Berachot 24a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:2: Regarding hearing idle talk, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Ketubot 5a): what is [the meaning of] "and you shall have a peg (yated) [for you outside the camp]" (Deuteronomy 23:14)? That if a person hears an improper matter, he should place his finger in his ears — this being why Rabbi Elazar said: why are a person's fingers like pegs? What is the reason? If it is to separate them, each one for its own purpose, as the master said, this is the pinky, this is the ring finger, this is the middle finger, this is the index finger, and this is the thumb — but why is it that their tips are sloped like pegs? So that if he hears something improper he can place his finger in his ears. And it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: why is the outer part of the ear hard and the earlobe soft? So that if he hears something improper he can bend the earlobe into it [to block it]. Our Rabbis taught: a person should not let improper words be heard by his ears, because they are the first to be scorched among the limbs — so far their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:3: Likewise one must be careful not to listen to evil speech (lashon hara) and not to accept it, for one who accepts it is worse than one who speaks it, as will be explained. Further, one must be careful not to be like one whose "ear is stopped up from the cry [of the poor]" (Proverbs 21:13).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:4: Further, one must be careful regarding what the prophet Isaiah, peace be upon him, said, among the good qualities that the Sages enumerated (Makkot 24a), which are the foundations of the Torah and the commandments — one of them being (Isaiah 33:15), "who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed" — such as Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, and the story is told in Bava Metzia (84b); from there is great proof that he would not remain silent when he heard the disparagement of Torah scholars.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:5: Further, one must be careful, if he has already heard a matter of halachah or midrash, and now hears it again for a second time, not to turn his ear away from hearing it and say, "I have already heard this" — for concerning this it is said, "whoever turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" (Proverbs 28:9). And so it is explained in the Midrash (Yalkut Mishlei, remez 937), on the verse, "let her breasts satisfy you at all times" (Proverbs 5:19), in these words: "let her breasts satisfy you at all times" — so that you not say, "we heard this last year," as it is said, "do not despise your mother when she is old" (Proverbs 23:22); and if you say this, I too can say to you, why do you recite the Shema twice a day, why do you pray three times a day — perhaps you are innovating something new [each time]? If you have mocked words of Torah, I too will not hear your prayer, as it is said, "whoever turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" — so far their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:6: Further, among the things that blemish the sense of hearing is if one lets his voice be heard by another while praying the Amidah silently; and besides what they said in the Gemara (Berachot 24b), that this shows a deficiency of faith, they elaborate at length on the punishment for this in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel 209a), in these words: then a certain officer stationed on the south side is aroused, whose name is Azriel the Elder, and sometimes called Machniel, because he is appointed over sixty myriads of camps, all masters of wings, masters of camps full of eyes; and opposite them stand those camps who are masters of ears, called "ears" because they listen to all those who pray their prayers in a whisper, with the will of the heart, so that that prayer is not heard by another — that prayer ascends and is heard by all those called masters of ears. But if that prayer is heard by a person's [own] ears [i.e., audible to others], no one above listens to it, and no others hear it except the one who heard it first — therefore one must be careful that people not hear that prayer; and further, the matter of prayer is bound up with the supernal world, and a matter of the supernal world should not be heard. And it further says on: when that prayer ascends in a whisper, all those sixty myriads of camps, and all those masters of eyes, and all those listening masters of ears, all go out and kiss that word of prayer that ascends — this is what is written, "the eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous, and His ears toward their cry" (Psalms 34:16) — "the eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous" — these are the masters of eyes below, since there are masters of eyes above; "and His ears toward their cry" — these are the masters of ears — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:7: Further, among the rectifications of the ear is that if he has heard a secret, he should not reveal it, as is explained in the Idra (Parashat Ha'azinu 294b), in these words: in this ear hang supernal mysteries that do not go outward; therefore it is bent inward, and the mystery of mysteries is concealed; woe to him who reveals mysteries; and because this ear grasps the mysteries and depths within, it does not reveal mysteries to those who are twisted in their ways, but only to those who are not twisted — this is what is written, "the secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him, and He will make known to them His covenant" (Psalms 25:14) — [i.e., those] who guard His ways and guard words — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:8: Further, it explains there, adjacent to this passage, that the sense of hearing is connected to the eyes, the nose, and the mouth, in these words: with this cavity of the ears are connected other cavities — the cavities of the eyes, the cavity of the mouth, the cavity of the nose. From that voice that enters the cavity of the ears, if it needs to, it enters the cavities of the eyes and tears well up from that voice; if it needs to, it enters the cavity of the nostrils, which is the nose, and smoke and fire emerge from that voice — this is what is written, "and the Lord heard, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burned among them" (Numbers 11:1); and if it needs to, that voice enters the cavity of the mouth, and it speaks and decrees decrees from that voice — all of it, from that voice, enters the whole body and is felt from it. On what does this depend? On this ear. Fortunate is he who guards his words; therefore it is written, "guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit" (Psalms 34:14) — so far his words. His words are understood according to the plain sense, though they certainly contain an inner mystical dimension.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:9: By this we understand what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Kamma 85b), that one who deafens another [in an injury case] pays him full damages, because all his limbs are found idle [i.e., his whole life is diminished]. According to his words, the blemish of speech and the blemish of hearing occur together as one; and this is what he was precise about at the end of his words, saying, "therefore it is written, 'guard your tongue from evil...'" — for if he speaks evil, that voice enters the ears and shakes the whole body and decrees decrees, and so on — this is [the meaning of] "and the Lord heard, and His anger was kindled..."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:10: From here a person can see how great a blemish comes to one who hears evil speech and idle words and other blemishing things with his ears; and therefore it says (Ketubot 5b) that he should bend the earlobe inward, so that the other senses not be damaged, particularly in light of what is explained there in the Idra, that Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at are comprised within hearing. And if he speaks evil speech about his fellow and the like, besides the blemish of speech, he causes his fellow to sin through the blemish of hearing, and also causes "the Lord to hear and His anger to be kindled."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:11: In the Tikkunim (122a) it says that the essential aspect of hearing is on the left, and therefore, if he lets his voice be heard, it should be with awe. In these words: hearing [belongs to] those who fear God, and concerning it is said, "incline Your ear, O Lord, and hear" (II Kings 19:16), and there is the awe and dread of Isaac; this is what is written, "O Lord, I have heard Your report and I was afraid" (Habakkuk 3:2). And whoever lets his voice be heard, whether in Torah or in prayer or in a cry, without awe, immediately "and the Lord heard, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burned among them" — and there are how many guardians of the gates there, called "the ears of the Lord" — so far his words. Here are all the negative aspects that depend on hearing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:12: There are positive aspects too, explained in the Tikkunim (131b): they said, of blessed memory: and there are commandments that depend on hearing, such as the recitation of the Shema, or other commandments of which it is said (Berachot 15a), "if he made it audible to his own ear, he has fulfilled his obligation" — and this refers to the blowing of the shofar — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:13: And in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas 228-229) it says that the rectification of hearing has three aspects: whether hearing the eighteen blessings from the prayer leader and answering "Amen" to each and every blessing; or hearing the reading of the Torah scroll from the reader; or hearing his colleague's reasoning in a matter of halachah. In these words: the third rectification is those who listen to the Torah scroll at the time speech goes forth from the mouth of the reader — this is considered for them as though they receive the Torah at Mount Sinai; and at the time He says, "I am [the Lord your God]" (Anochi), no other voice or speech of any living creature is heard except His. In this same manner, when speech goes forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the fiery living creatures are silent, and at the time the fiery living creatures are silent, they speak [in their own way] — this is what is written, "and all the people saw the voices" (Exodus 20:15) — the voices of the living creatures that were roaring — "and the torches" that emerged in speech from the living creatures in several kinds of song before the King. These, who listen to the Torah scroll, are the image of the living creatures, and the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints them to enter into the chamber of the vision of fire, His house. Further, those who listen in prayer to the eighteen blessings shall enter into the chamber of this vision. Further, those who listen to a matter of halachah, of which it is said, "the reward for [studying] the tradition is [in] the reasoning [derived]," shall enter into the chamber that is the palace of this vision — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:14: Further, in the Tikkunim (63a), in these words: the fourth offering — this is the one who receives the offering, corresponding to Adam, who is Thought, who offers and unifies everything; concerning him it is said, "When a man (adam) among you brings an offering" (Leviticus 1:2) — this is the one who brings an offering to the Lord, and this is the Torah; and therefore they established, in prayer, the [custom of] hearing the Torah scroll, so that it become a complete offering in Adam — of whom it is said, "this is the Torah, adam" (Numbers 19:14). And therefore, "whoever turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" — so far their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:15: Included in this rectification: sometimes it happens that during the reading of the Torah or during prayer, a man speaks with his fellow about worldly matters, and he stops listening to the Torah or prayer in order to hear that matter — for one must not incline his ear to hear anything except that thing to which he originally set his intention to listen, and even if they speak words of Torah, he should not incline his ear, since "hearing is like answering," and during the reading of the Torah or during the prayer leader's repetition of the prayer, it is forbidden for him to occupy himself with Torah, as is explained in the passage. The general rule is that one should not mix one rectification with another, for each has its own separate time — all the more so if he mixes mundane with holy, for then the blemish is great.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:16: Further, regarding the rectification of hearing, it is explained in the Tikkunim (122a), in these words: and therefore one must clear the hair away from the ears, so that the gates of hearing prayer not be blocked — for through them He hears prayers, He of whom it is said, "O You who hears prayer, unto You shall all flesh come" (Psalms 65:3) — so far their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:17: The blemish to the sense of smell, which is the nose — there is no doubt that anger and wrath are what blemish it, as they say in the Zohar (Parashat Tetzaveh 182a), "Cease from man, whose breath (neshamah) is in his nostrils" (Isaiah 2:22). Likewise, one should not derive benefit from the scent of idolatry or forbidden foods. Likewise one should distance himself from the scent of a married woman's garments, since it will arouse in him evil desire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:18: The rectification of smell is said there in the Tikkunim (131b), in these words: and all the offerings that are "a pleasing odor unto the Lord" depend on the nose, and the fragrant woods of the incense — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:19: It seems to me that now, because of our sins, when we have no offering, the words of our lips ascend in place of the scent, as is known, as they explained, of blessed memory (see Menachot 110a): "this is the Torah of the burnt offering, of the meal offering, and of the sin offering..." (Leviticus 7:37) — whoever occupies himself with the Torah [passage] of the burnt offering, it is as though he offered a burnt offering, and so on. Just as, through the scent of the offering, satisfaction was given above, as explained in the Idra (Parashat Ha'azinu 294a), regarding the nose of Ze'ir [Anpin], "and the Lord smelled the sweet savor" (Genesis 8:21) — it does not say "the scent of the offering" but "the sweet savor," for all the powers of Gevurah that grasp hold of the nose, and all that are attached to them, are all sweetened. And it says further on that upon the altar the fire and the smoke rising from the two nostrils would be sweetened, and the nose of Arich [Anpin] would be revealed, concerning whom it is said, "and My praise I hold back for you" (Isaiah 48:9), as is likewise explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach 70a) — see there. And if a person sins with anger and wrath, giving room for the powers of Gevurah to spread, through his occupation with Torah they will be sweetened and comprised in their source, and the supernal mercies will be revealed to sweeten everything. How good it would be if he is fasting, so that the scent rising from his mouth is in place of an offering, and through the breath of Torah his mouth's scent will ascend above to unify and sweeten the judgments — for the breath of Torah is a ladder for the ascent of prayer and the ascent of the soul, as will be explained in the Gate of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:20: And if he intends, in his reading, the act of the offering — that it ascend before the supernal Man, which is the mystery of Thought, Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, who unifies everything, as explained above — it may also help to rectify one's thoughts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:21: Further, regarding the rectification of smell, they say in the Tikkunim (122a), in these words: scent — there, the men of truth [are found]; and there ascend all the scents, incense, and smoke of offerings, and prayers that are considered like offerings; and if a person does not raise them with love and awe, what is written of him? "For then the anger of the Lord shall smoke, and His jealousy against that man" (Deuteronomy 29:19) — so far his words. From this passage there is proof for our intent — for it says that prayer, which is in place of an offering, ascends to the nose of Ze'ir [Anpin] to make a pleasing scent, when a person prays that prayer with awe and love; but if not, God forbid, because of the side of judgment that it arouses, "then the anger of the Lord shall smoke," and so on — all the more so one who occupies himself with the Torah [passage] of an offering, that it ascend as a pleasing scent to rectify the judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:22: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, was further precise in his wording, saying, "and there ascend all the scents, incense, and so on" — the intent being that the incense (ketoret) too used to ascend to this place to sweeten judgment, and also if a person recites [the passage of] the incense with intention, it ascends to this place to rectify and sweeten the judgments. At the end of Parashat Vayakhel (218b) they elaborate on the greatness of the incense, and we shall quote its wording regarding prayer — from there too there is proof for our intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:23: What it says, "and if not, [one should] raise them with love and awe," whereas above regarding hearing it mentioned only awe alone — the reason is that smell is on the middle line, as it says, "scent — there, the men of truth [are found]" — and the attribute of Truth unifies the left and the right, which are awe and love; therefore the rectification of the scent of prayer, and everything that ascends to the nose, is through both awe and love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:24: And with this, this chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:1: Now that we have explained, in the preceding chapters, sight, hearing, and smell, which correspond to Yod-Heh-Vav, lion, ox, eagle, as we quoted from the wording of Rashbi at the beginning of chapter 8, let us now explain speech, which corresponds to the final Heh, and is the face of Man.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:2: The wording of Rashbi there (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas 234a): speech — Man; it grasps above and below. The explanation of these words is explained in what is explained in the Tikkunim (122a), regarding the four rectifications — sight, hearing, smell, speech — where it explains that sight is to the right, lion; hearing to the left, ox; smell in the middle, eagle. And it says afterward, in these words: the mouth — this is Man, comprising the four letters and comprising the ten letters, and this is the Shechinah — so far his words. "Comprising the four letters" is the Name YHVH, and "[comprising the ten letters]" is Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, as is likewise explained (129a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:3: The matter can be further understood from what is said in the Tikkunim (there, 63a): that lion, ox, eagle are sight, hearing, smell, and upon them rests the face of the supernal Man, which is the mystery of Thought; and afterward it says, at the end of its words, "speech — this is Man, who comprises them all — who brings it forth? Thought" — so far his words. Through this passage the two preceding passages can be understood — what it said on page 121, that speech is the Shechinah, and this is in the mystery of the simple Name and the Name spelled out to equal ten. This is indeed the truth — that the Name is simple, in that she comprises the three faces, which are lion, ox, eagle, Yod-Heh-Vav within her, she being the final Heh; and the Name is spelled out to ten, this being from the mystery of the supernal Thought, as I elaborated above in chapter 6. It follows likewise that speech grasps above and below — above in the mystery of Thought, and below in the Shechinah — this is the general understanding of the matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:4: In particular terms, it is that a person cannot speak unless he first thinks of what he will say — it is necessary that the speech first be portrayed in thought — and when he speaks, the power of thought goes forth with that speech; therefore speech necessarily contains both aforementioned Names together, and this is the mystery of "the Lord founded the earth with Chochmah" (Proverbs 3:19). Therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (83a), in these words: Yod is saying, speech, and calling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:5: However, it is difficult for me [to reconcile] what is said in the Tikkunim, page 3 (3a), that speech is the Name Adonai. One might say that what is said in the passage before us regarding YHVH being both simple and spelled-out is entirely the aspect of "voice" (kol) [rather than "speech" (dibbur)] — and this requires further study.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:6: To understand the matter properly, it will be explained by what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar Parashat Noach 74a) on the verse, "and the house, when it was built, was built of stone made ready before it was brought there" (I Kings 6:7) — he explains this verse regarding the matter of speech, from where its root is, and explains that its root is from the mystery of Thought. He says: when it arises in the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, to make honor for His glory, will arises from within Thought to spread out, and so on. And he describes the reality of the spreading of Atzilut until it becomes "voice," and says: from where — from Thought that was concealed, silent, it becomes heard, to be revealed. Further, this Thought spreads out to be revealed, and this voice strikes and knocks against the lips, and then speech emerges and completes everything and reveals everything; it becomes heard that everything is that concealed Thought that was within, and all is one — once this spreading-out reaches [the point] that speech is made with the strength of that voice, then "and the house, when it was built" — it does not say "as it was built," and so on — so far his words, as pertains to us. Whoever wishes to delve deeper into the mystery of this matter should examine the passage in its place there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:7: Similarly, it says in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi 246b), regarding "Naphtali is a hind let loose, he gives (hanoten) goodly words" (Genesis 49:21) — it explains this verse in the mystery of speech, and raises the difficulty that it should have said "hanotenet" [feminine form, since "hind" is feminine]. It resolves: come and see, Thought is the beginning of everything, and so on, and at the end of its words it says: and when you look at the levels, it is Thought, it is Binah, it is Voice, it is Speech, and all is one; and it is Thought, the beginning of everything, and there is no separation, but all is one, one bond, which is literally Thought, bound in the Infinite (Ein Sof), and never separates. This is [the meaning of] "the Lord is one and His Name is one" (Zechariah 14:9); and therefore it is written "hanoten" (he gives), [in the masculine] — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:8: Through the reason of this alluded mystery we understand what is said in the Zohar (Parashat Chukat 183b) — that whoever guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in the holy spirit. In these words: "and Esther put on royalty" (Esther 5:1) — she was clothed in the supernal holy royalty, certainly she wore the holy spirit; why did she merit this level? Because she guarded her mouth so as not to reveal anything, this being what is written, "Esther did not reveal her kindred" (Esther 2:20); and we learn that whoever guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in a holy spirit — so far his words. And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, beginning of 61) it explains that when she [Malchut] is called "the holy spirit," it is when she nurses from the mystery of Chochmah. In these words, in brief: and this "zot" (Malchut), when she is blessed, is called "holy" and is called "Chochmah," and she is called "the holy spirit" — meaning, a spirit from that supernal holiness — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:9: The reason for the term "clothing" — that one who guards his tongue merits the holy spirit — is explained by what is explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso 134a), in the rectifications of the supernal Beard, twelfth rectification, which says that the holy spirit emerging from the supernal mouth is that in which Ze'ir Anpin is clothed, and from this spirit all those below are clothed, and so on. And it further says: and therefore the spirit that goes outward, in which the faithful prophets are clothed, is called "the fruit of the Lord"; but in this Ancient of Ancients it does not separate, and there is none who knows His spirit except He Himself — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:10: From here you can know how great is the level of one who guards the breath of wind emerging from his mouth, for it alludes to a supernal place, and therefore he merits to be clothed in the holy spirit. Concerning one who guards his spirit it is said, "but he that has a faithful spirit conceals the matter" (Proverbs 11:13). "Faithful" is explained as being strong in his spirit, so as not to release it in a place unfit — the word "faithful" (ne'eman) is explained as in "and I will fasten him as a peg in a sure (ne'eman) place" (Isaiah 22:23) — meaning, strong, without collapsing. The reverse of this is, "a fool utters (yotzi) all his spirit" (Proverbs 29:11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:11: The punishment for one who blemishes the breath emerging from his mouth is explained by what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach 59a), regarding "all is vanity (hevel) and vexation of spirit" (Ecclesiastes 1:14). It says there that we cannot say that this "hevel" mentioned in the verse refers to something in Atzilut, in the mystery of the seven "breaths" (havalim) that exist above in Atzilut, called "the utterance of the mouth of the Lord," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria 47b) — for if it referred to that, it would not be "vexation of spirit"; rather, the explanation is that it refers to the external forces. In these words: come and see, at the hour deeds are made fit below, and a person considers the service of the holy King, that matter he performs becomes a "hevel" (breath) [that rises] from him above, and there is no "hevel" that does not have a voice that ascends and is crowned above and becomes a defender before the Holy One, blessed be He. But all those deeds a person occupies himself with that are not the service of the Holy One, blessed be He — that matter he performs becomes a "hevel" that goes and roams the world; and when a person's soul departs, that "hevel" tosses it about in the world like a stone in a sling, as it is written, "and the souls of your enemies, He shall sling out, as from the hollow of a sling" (I Samuel 25:29). Who slings it out? That "hevel" that speaks around it in the world. Then all the things done, which are under the sun, that are not the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, become a "hevel" from them — "hevel" is the breaking of the spirit, that breaks the spirit and ascends and descends in the world — this is what is written, "hevel and vexation of spirit." But that matter which is the service of one's Master is called "above the sun," and from it is made a holy "hevel" — and this is the seed that a person sows in that world; and what is its name? Righteousness (tzedakah), as it is written, "sow for yourselves according to righteousness" (Hosea 10:12). This is what speaks for a person when his soul leaves him and ascends to be found in the place of glory above, to be bound in the bundle of life — this is what is written, "and your righteousness shall go before you" (Isaiah 58:8), to speak for you, to raise you from place to place, as it is written, "the glory of the Lord shall gather you" (Isaiah 58:8) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:12: Here it is explained in this passage that every improper deed produces a "hevel" that clothes the soul and slings it into the sling — and this is "vexation of spirit" — and this is what it is precise about, saying, "who slings it out? That 'hevel' that speaks around it in the world" — and in saying "around the world," it hints at the alluded mystery of this matter. All the more so when the "hevel" emerging from his mouth is in vain, in falsehood, and the like, for it goes to the place of this evil "hevel," which is "vexation of spirit," and from it a garment is made to clothe his spirit and sling it into the sling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:13: In the Tikkunim (117b) Rashbi explains the mystery of the "havalim" (breaths) on the side of holiness and the "havalim" on the side of the kelipah. He says there that there is a good "hevel" and an evil "hevel": the "hevel" of Torah, which is a flame (lahav), concerning which it is said, "the voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire" (Psalms 29:7), and this "hevel" is on the right side, comprising seven "havalim" corresponding to the seven Names within the Forty-Two-Letter Name, Aleph-Bet-Gimel Yod-Tav-Tzadi, and so on. He says: six ascend, which are the flames in the six rings of the windpipe, and the seventh "hevel" of the mouth; and corresponding to these David said, "seven voices, give unto the Lord, O sons of the mighty" (cf. Psalms 29:1); and concerning these seven it is said, "for man does not live by bread alone, but by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord does man live" (Deuteronomy 8:3); and these seven voices ascend into seven firmaments. And there are seven of the left that descend into seven lands, and concerning them Kohelet says, "for who knows whether the spirit of the sons of man ascends upward..." (Ecclesiastes 3:21) (the explanation is regarding the end of the verse, "and the spirit of the animal descends downward to the earth"). Seven good breaths — these are the seven days of the week corresponding to them; and others corresponding to the seven years of famine — these are breaths of life and those are breaths of death, and therefore there is a "hevel" [singular] and there are "havalim" [plural] — so far his words.
